knowledge_point.title: Evaluating the Derivative at a Point Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(\mathbf{r}(t))]$ at $t=1$ given that $∇f(x,y)=\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{4}{y}\right)\,\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{r}(t)=\left(4 t^{2} + 2\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,\mathbf{j}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(\mathbf{r}(t))]=∇f(\mathbf{r}(t))\cdot {\mathbf{r}}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{4}{y}\right)\,\mathbf{j}.
$$

First, we substitute $x=4 t^{2} + 2$ and $y=\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(\mathbf{r}(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(\mathbf{r}(t)) & =\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{4}{y}\right)\,\mathbf{j}\Big|_{x=4 t^{2} + 2,\,y=\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}} \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{4}{\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}}\right)\,\mathbf{j}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $\mathbf{r}(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(4 t^{2} + 2\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,\mathbf{j} \\  & =\left(8 t\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{1}{t^{2} + 1}\right)\,\mathbf{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(\mathbf{r}(t))] & =∇f(\mathbf{r}(t))\cdot {\mathbf{r}}^{′}(t) \\  & =\left(\left(\frac{1}{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{4}{\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}}\right)\,\mathbf{j}\right)\cdot \left(\left(8 t\right)\,\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{1}{t^{2} + 1}\right)\,\mathbf{j}\right) \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}\right)\cdot \left(8 t\right)+\left(\frac{4}{\operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}}\right)\cdot \left(\frac{1}{t^{2} + 1}\right) \\  & =\left(\frac{4 t}{2 t^{2} + 1}\right)+\left(\frac{4}{t^{2} \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)} + \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}}\right) \\  & =\frac{4 \left(t^{3} \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)} + 2 t^{2} + t \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)} + 1\right)}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right) \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right) \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(\mathbf{r}(t))]\Big|_{t=1} & =\frac{4 \left(t^{3} \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)} + 2 t^{2} + t \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)} + 1\right)}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right) \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right) \operatorname{atan}{\left(t \right)}}\Big|_{t=1} \\  & =\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{8}{\pi}\right) \\  & =\frac{4 \left(\pi + 6\right)}{3 \pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real; all displayed denominators nonzero; square-root path t>0.
